point_description: Sarah's forever routine: microcurrent, vitamin C, azelaic acid, daily SPF, LED, tretinoin recovery nights, and a bedtime slugging ritual.

am.title: Cleanse
am.product: Balea MED Ultra Sensitive Wash Gel
am.description:
I like to use a gentle cleanser in the morning, even though you technically don't need to cleanse in the am unless you feel very greasy or sweaty, it is fine to skip cleanser to keep the barrier calm.

When you do cleanse, keep it gentle and non-stripping. Since I am close to the German border I can easily get to a dm, I love their brand Balea for affordable skin and haircare. This Balea MED wash gel is boring in the best way, sensitive-skin friendly, and not trying to do too much.

am.title: Rose Water Spray
am.product: Mario Badescu Facial Spray with Aloe, Herbs and Rosewater
am.description: Mist after cleansing or as the first step if skipping cleanser. Damp skin makes the next watery layers spread more evenly, and the ritual part matters too: it makes the routine feel less like homework.

am.title: Microcurrent
am.description:
Use NuFACE for about five minutes with NuFACE Hydrating Aqua Gel Activator or another conductive gel. The gel matters because microcurrent needs slip and conductivity; do not try to drag the device over dry skin.

I like this step in the morning because the instant lifted look is wasted on a pillow. If I'm in a hurry, this is one of the steps I skip.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description:
This is a Polish brand that I'm trying out for the first time with this Vitamin C serum. Of course there are plenty of alternatives on the market, at various price ranges and stabilities. I will have to do a whole blog post on Vitamin C serums to explain, but in a nutshell, don't go for the cheapest option and make sure you keep it in a cool dark place. I keep this one in the fridge.

Vitamin C is the brightening and an antioxidant step in the morning routine.

am.title: Azelaic Acid
am.description:
Azelaic acid is one of those quiet workhorse ingredients. I use this one from France at 15%, but there are easier to get alternatives in the US at lower concentrations like The INKEY List SuperSolutions 10% Azelaic Serum Redness Relief Solution. In Poland they have a 20% OTC that I want to try once I'm finished with my tube of Azéane.

Use as the pigment, redness, and texture-support step after vitamin C if your skin is tolerating the combination. If skin feels reactive, use this less often or separate it from other actives. Consistency matters more than forcing it every single morning.

am.title: Moisturizer
am.description:
Use only if skin needs it, especially in winter or when the routine feels a little too active. This is not mandatory every morning; it is the comfort layer when your skin is asking for one.

Keep it light so SPF can still sit properly on top.

am.title: Face Oil & Gua Sha
am.description:
Use a face oil for slip, then gua sha with gentle upward and outward strokes. There are many gua sha shapes, but I like this kind of square shape best vs the triangle. I've linked the tarte Maracuja oil but really I have a proprietary blend that I'll have to write a post about soon.

This step belongs before SPF. Oil after sunscreen can disturb the protective film, so finish any massage before moving on to the final sunscreen layer.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap around the eye area before face SPF. Many sunscreens sting around the eyes, but this one does not so this keeps the eye area protected without making the whole morning miserable.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: SPF
am.product: La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVMune 400 Anti-Dark Spots Fluid SPF50+
am.description:
SPF is always last. Do not layer oil, moisturizer, or gua sha on top of this because it can interfere with the sunscreen film. If you can only do one thing in the morning, it is sunscreen. This is the non-negotiable step for dark spots, sun damage, and keeping the rest of the routine worth doing.

I am currently looking to replace my beloved Josie Maran SPF that was discontinued. Sadly this one is not a good replacement, read my full review on it here.

am.title: Lip Balm
am.description:
I have always had a love/hate relationship with lip balm, my lips seemed addicted to it and yet still irritated. Then I discovered beef tallow balm, Hudsalva is great because it avoids the beeswax and petrolatum feel that can make lips angry instead of comfortable. I read an interview with Alicia Vikander who swears by it so I had to try it. It is sold at a pharmacy in Sweden and at Boots in the UK according to her.

I used to be able to find it on Amazon, but once that became unreliable I found this US-based option by Vintage Tradition.

pm.description: A double cleanse with an oil cleanser is a great way to wash off makeup and sunscreen. I start with SKIN1004 Madagascar Centella Light Cleansing Oil, then I follow with Tatcha The Deep Cleanse.

pm.title: LED Mask
pm.product: Solawave Wrinkle Retreat Pro LED Face Mask
pm.description:
Use on clean, dry skin before leave-on skincare. LED fits best here because it gets a bare-skin window and does not have to fight through oil, slugging layers, or sunscreen.

This linked mask is a U.S. brand, Solawave's current Wrinkle Retreat Pro LED Face Mask, but I use a European LED mask by Koanna. Any LED mask with at least 630–660 nm red and 810–850 nm near-infrared works.

pm.title: Treatment
pm.description:

Because tretinoin is prescription-only, the link goes to Differin Gel as a popular over-the-counter retinoid option. French A313 is another well-known retinoid-style option. On recovery nights, skip retinoids and use The Ordinary Multi-Peptide + Copper Peptides 1% Serum instead.

pm.title: Rose Water Spray
pm.product: Mario Badescu Facial Spray with Aloe, Herbs and Rosewater
pm.description: Mist after the treatment has had a few minutes to settle. This brings back a little dampness before hydrating serum, which helps the next step spread without tugging.

pm.title: Hydrating Serum
pm.description:
Apply a hydrating serum while skin is slightly damp from the rose water. This is the cushion step that makes the retinoid routine feel less austere.

The Ordinary hyaluronic acid works here, or you can swap in Celimax Noni Ampoule when you want a more soothing, plush serum.

pm.title: Eye Cream
pm.product: Beauty of Joseon Revive Eye Serum : Ginseng + Retinal
pm.description: I have so many favorite eye creams for evening but this is what I am currently using. As long as it has a retinoid I am willing to try it. This one is very nice and refreshing, perfect for summer since it isn't heavy. Of course, one of my favs my Glow Recipe was discontinued (the Avocado Melt Reintol Eye Cream). I've also tried the budget option by Inkey List but it is kind of lumpy and not smooth or premium feeling at all.

pm.title: Moisturizer
pm.description: Use as the main moisturizer before oil. Embryolisse gives the routine a soft, reliable buffer, especially after tretinoin or on nights when skin needs the extra comfort.

pm.title: Face Oil & Gua Sha
pm.product: The Ordinary 100% Organic Cold-Pressed Rose Hip Seed Oil
pm.description:
Use homemade night oil for slip, then gua sha with gentle upward and outward strokes. The linked Ordinary rosehip oil is the straightforward store-bought comparison.

This is the massage and sealant step before the bedtime slugging layers. Give it a little time if you can.

pm.title: More Hyaluronic Acid
pm.description: Use as part one of the bedtime slugging routine. By this point, some time has usually passed after face oil, so Ialuset acts like the plush humectant layer before the final occlusive seal.

pm.title: Slugging Balm
pm.description: Use as the final face layer to seal in all the moisture. This is the true occlusive finish of the bedtime slugging routine: everything hydrating goes underneath, Egyptian Magic locks it down.

pm.title: Lip Mask
pm.description: Finish with the Laneige lip mask. It stays cushiony overnight, which is exactly what you want from the final lip step before bed. My lips are never dry in the morning.

am.title: Rinse
am.description: In her streamlined morning routine, Hailey starts with the basics: a splash of water to rinse away the remnants of her nighttime skin care. This keeps the morning cleanse gentle, which makes sense for the dry, sensitive skin she has described.

am.title: Mist
am.description:
Use this as the first hydrating step after rinsing. Hailey said that when she is really busy in the morning, she can literally spray her face with this and walk out the door.

Rhode describes it as a hydrating face spray that can be used after cleansing, after moisturizer, or whenever skin needs a refresh.

am.title: Essence
am.description:
Press a generous amount onto the face, neck, and décolleté. Hailey calls Glazing Milk one of her staple products and says she uses it in the morning, at night, and as skin prep.

Rhode recommends applying it after morning or evening cleansing, before Peptide Glazing Fluid and moisturizer.

am.title: Peptide Serum
am.description:
Apply 2-3 pumps to the face, neck, and décolleté. Hailey's 2022 Vogue routine centered on hydration because she has dry, sensitive skin, and this peptide serum was part of that routine.

Rhode recommends following this step with Barrier Restore Cream or Barrier Butter for best results.

am.title: Moisturizer
am.description:
Apply as the barrier-supporting moisturizer step. Rhode recommends using about a half finger-length amount on the face, neck, and décolleté.

am.title: SPF
am.description: Use generously as the final morning skin-care step. Hailey says sunscreen is non-negotiable, and Vogue noted that she likes milky SPF formulas and fell in love with ISDIN Fusion Water Magic SPF on a trip to Paris.

am.title: Lip Treatment
am.description: Glaze lips during the day and reapply whenever they need hydration. In her Vogue routine, Hailey said she does not leave the house without a lip product, morning or night.

pm.title: Oil Cleanse

pm.description: Massage onto dry skin to break down SPF and makeup, then rinse. In her nighttime routine, Hailey said oil cleansing was a newer addition that made a big difference, and she prefers it over makeup wipes.

pm.title: Hydrating Cleanse
pm.product: HoliFrog Tashmoo Water Lily Milky Wash
pm.description: Follow the oil cleanse with a gentle, hydrating cleanser. Hailey said she does not love a super-foaming cleanser and prefers a richer option that does not leave dry, sensitive skin feeling stripped.

pm.title: Essence
pm.description: Press into clean skin before serum. Hailey says she uses Glazing Milk at night too, and Vogue noted that she likes it even when using stronger nighttime products because it helps buffer irritation and support hydration.

pm.title: Peptide Serum
pm.description:
Apply 2-3 pumps and press it in gently. Hailey's newer Rhode-era routines center this peptide serum as a hydrating, barrier-supporting step.

In her earlier 2021 nighttime routine, she also mentioned using Biba Los Angeles Plant Stem Cell Peptide Serum and emphasized that she is a big fan of peptides.

pm.title: Rich Moisturizer
pm.description:

pm.title: Face Oil
pm.product: Furtuna Skin Due Alberi Biphase Moisturizing Oil
pm.description: Use only if skin is very dry. Hailey layered a thin amount of face oil for extra glow and hydration, but she also noted that she avoids heavier oils when she is actively breaking out.

pm.title: Pimple Patches
pm.description: Use on active pimples only. Hailey said she likes sleeping in these when she is breaking out because they help a pimple heal faster, and she also likes that they look cute.

pm.description:

pm.description:
Finish with Aquaphor on the lips. Hailey said she legitimately cannot go to bed without lip balm because she hates chapped, dry lips, and Aquaphor is her go-to.

She also uses a little extra Aquaphor on flaky dry patches when needed.

point_description: A low-fuss routine that puts the money where it matters: daily sunscreen, a beginner retinol, vitamin C, and enough barrier support to keep going.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description: The first step is having a clean palette for the rest of the routine. A nice, boring, gentle cleanser will prepare your skin for what comes next. If your skin is dry and clean in the morning, it is also completely fine to just rinse with water.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.product: CeraVe Skin Renewing Vitamin C Serum
am.description: Apply a thin layer to dry skin before moisturizer. This gives you a straightforward 10% vitamin C step with ceramides and panthenol, for brightening and antioxidant support.

am.title: Moisturize
am.description: Use one to two pumps after vitamin C. It has ceramides, squalane, and hyaluronic acid, and it plays nicely with actives. This is not the glamorous step, it is the compliance step: comfortable skin is much more likely to stick with sunscreen and retinol.

am.title: SPF
am.product: Neutrogena Invisible Daily Defense Face Serum SPF 60+
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step to face, ears, neck, chest, and hands. This is the most important anti-aging product in the routine because prevention beats trying to undo UV damage later.

If you'd like a drugstore mineral option, try CeraVe Hydrating Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50, though untinted mineral formulas can leave a cast. For a tinted mineral option, Neutrogena Purescreen+ Mineral UV Tint SPF 30 is more wearable and comes in multiple shades.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.product: e.l.f. Holy Hydration! Makeup Melting Cleansing Balm
pm.description: Use this first on dry skin when you wore makeup, water-resistant sunscreen, or just a lot of SPF. Massage it in until sunscreen and makeup feel loosened, then emulsify with a little water and rinse. This is the step that makes the gentle cleanser actually stand a chance without scrubbing your face like you are mad at it.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.description: Follow the balm with a gentle water-based cleanser. This removes any leftover film and gives you clean skin before retinol without chasing that squeaky-clean feeling.

pm.title: Retinol
pm.description:
Start two nights a week, using a thin layer over the face while avoiding eyelids, lip edges, and the creases beside the nose. This is a gentle drugstore retinol with ceramides and niacinamide, so it fits the point of this routine: effective enough to matter, boring enough that your skin may actually tolerate it.

If you are sensitive, sandwich it between two thin layers of moisturizer. Once tolerated every other night, a dermatologist-prescribed tretinoin is the evidence-maximizing upgrade.

pm.title: Moisturize
pm.description: Finish with moisturizer. If your skin feels tight or flaky, use more moisturizer rather than adding more actives. The goal is steady use over months, not heroic peeling in week one.

point_description: A mid-tier routine for someone who wants the same evidence-based bones with nicer textures: barrier care, vitamin C, SPF, and retinal.

am.title: Cleanse

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description: Apply a few drops to dry skin in the morning. This is a 15% vitamin C serum, so it is a bit more ambitious than the drugstore tier. If it stings, use it every other morning or pause until the retinal routine is comfortable.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.description:
Apply a thin layer over vitamin C. This is where the routine buys a nicer daily experience: richer barrier support, a cushier finish, and enough comfort to make actives less annoying.

For oily skin, swap to Skinfix Skin Barrier Restoring Gel Cream or use a lighter layer.

am.title: SPF
am.description:
Use as the final morning step. This has that clear, primer-like finish people either love or hate (I'm honestly not the biggest fan).

If you prefer a mineral option, Supergoop Mineral Mattescreen SPF 40 has a subtle neutral tint to reduce cast, but the shade still needs to work for your skin tone.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.product: Farmacy Green Clean Makeup Removing Cleansing Balm
pm.description:
Use this as the first cleanse when you wore makeup, water-resistant SPF, or just need a more satisfying sunscreen removal step. Massage it onto dry skin, add water so it turns milky, then rinse before going in with your regular cleanser.

If your skin is very reactive, choose the fragrance-free version.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Use this as the second cleanse after balm, or as your only cleanser if you did not wear makeup and your sunscreen was easy to remove. Keep it practical: the goal is clean skin, not a stripped face.

pm.title: Retinal
pm.description:
Start two nights a week, then slowly build toward every other night if skin stays calm. Crystal Retinal 3 is positioned for newer vitamin A users and gives this tier a more elegant retinal step than the drugstore version.

Do not chase results by layering exfoliating acids on top. Slow and boring wins with retinoids.

pm.title: Barrier Cream
pm.description:
Finish with moisturizer, or sandwich the retinal between two thin layers if you are irritation-prone. A richer cream is not magic, but it can be the difference between quitting retinal and actually using it long enough to see results.

If your skin is oily or the cream feels heavy, use Skinfix Skin Barrier Restoring Gel Cream instead.

am.description: Apply four to five drops to dry skin in the morning. This is the luxury benchmark: 15% L-ascorbic acid with vitamin E and ferulic acid. It is expensive, iconic, and genuinely elegant, though less expensive vitamin C products still live in the same useful category.

am.title: Rich Cream
am.description: Apply a thin layer over vitamin C. This is the indulgent comfort step: deeply emollient, luxury-coded, and best for normal-to-dry skin. If you are combination or oily, Augustinus Bader The Cream is the lighter alternative.

am.title: Tinted Mineral SPF
am.description:
Use generously as the final morning step. The tint and iron oxides can add visible-light protection, which is especially useful for melasma and persistent hyperpigmentation, but the shade will not work for everyone.

Untinted alternatives: SkinCeuticals Clear Daily Soothing UV Defense SPF 50 has a sheer hydrating finish, and Skinbetter Sunbetter Sheer SPF 70 is an untinted mineral option, though it may leave a cast.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.description:
Use this as the first cleanse when you wore makeup, layered SPF, or anything water-resistant. Massage it onto dry skin, add water so it emulsifies, then rinse before your second cleanser.

This is the gentle luxury version of a cleansing balm: fragrance-free, cushiony, and made for sensitive or sensitized skin. Exactly the vibe you want before an AlphaRet night.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Use this as the second cleanse after balm, or as your only cleanse if you did not wear makeup and your sunscreen was easy to remove. Do not scrub, especially on AlphaRet nights.

pm.title: Retinoid
pm.description:
Start two nights a week and build slowly. AlphaRet combines a cosmetic retinoid with an AHA, so it is doing two active jobs at once. That can be beautiful for lines, pigment, and texture, but sensitive skin should move carefully.

Because this already contains exfoliating acid, do not add a separate peel during the adjustment period.

pm.title: Rich Cream
pm.description:
Finish with a thin layer, or use it before and after AlphaRet if skin needs buffering. This is a gorgeous experience step, but the unsexy truth remains: the results engine is still sunscreen plus retinoid consistency.

If The Rich Cream feels too heavy, swap to Augustinus Bader The Cream, the lighter version in the same product family.
